summary: Feed s115_double is degraded: IDS port overloaded by microbursts (1.71 Gbps on 1 Gbps port) and encrypted share 71.8% exceeds 60% tolerance, limiting payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate/burst traffic delivered to a single 1 Gbps IDS port exceeds capacity - 1.71 Gbps peaks in 1ms intervals (171% of port speed) across 7 intervals, typical of microbursts from aggregation without load balancing.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS will drop packets at ingress, causing missed signatures, broken flow reassembly and incomplete detection - needs_both_directions and needs_full_payload cannot be satisfied under drops.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across 2+ IDS ports/instances with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port rate <80% of 1 Gbps and preserve both directions per flow for stateful IDS inspection.

findings.root_cause: 71.8% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) vs IDS tolerance of 60%, so most payload is opaque to signature-based inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requiring full payload is blind to ~72% of traffic - cannot match signatures or detect intrusions inside encrypted sessions, sharply reducing detection coverage.

params.policy: decrypt or mirror decrypted copy to IDS where authorized

recommended_fix.why: Decrypting at the packet broker (or feeding a decrypted copy) restores payload visibility so the IDS can inspect content while respecting privacy/policy controls.
